requiredFindings.title: Charge or eliminate the encoder's digest-hex temporary allocations
requiredFindings.detail: push_row calls digest_hex for every inventory row. The imported helper is crates/identity/src/digests.rs::hex, which allocates String::with_capacity(64). Charging owned_record(inventory_len) pays for the inventory Vec, not these additional temporary strings; WorkLedger explicitly requires temporary copies to be charged separately. none_observation allocates another digest-hex string, and seal allocates the VCS digest string at line 356 in addition to the charged 160-byte VCS buffer. These are sealing-owned allocations outside the separately bounded IdentityCandidate admission, so LD-C1A3-4's every-allocation-before-it-happens claim is not met.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Write hex directly into the precharged destination, or use fixed stack arrays, to remove the temporary heap strings; alternatively charge every distinct temporary before allocation, including per-row and both VCS-path conversions. Add a focused accounting/allocation control that catches reintroducing an uncharged conversion. Update the sealing-charge evidence and any dependent r9 derivation if the charged terms change.

requiredFindings.title: Complete the mixed-error precedence controls required by C1A-T6
requiredFindings.detail: The accepted C1a r6 C1A-T6 requires an over-8-GiB inventory followed separately by a read I/O failure, a ChangedDuringRead failure, and a custody or open failure, each preceding the totalBytes refusal. walk_refusals_come_before_the_bounds injects only the later read I/O error. The zero-read synthetic step-5 bound tests and source pin showing no total bound in the walker are useful, but neither exercises the later changed-file or custody/open branches on an already over-bound inventory. SCOPE's structural explanation is also stronger than the API: SnapshotWalkReport is public, Default and Clone and is supplied separately from the session/root, so its type alone does not prove that it is this session's successful walk.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Keep the efficient split rather than writing 8 GiB: preload the synthetic reached over-bound capture, then add one later metadata-change case and one later custody/open-failure case through the actual session walk/sealing composition, asserting the original refusal and no sealing output. Retain the no-total source pin and exact step-5 bound controls. Describe successful-walk provenance as an explicit composition precondition unless the API enforces it; do not count the report's type as a structural proof.

nonBlockingObservations.title: Bind successful-walk provenance when the production composition is added
nonBlockingObservations.detail: seal accepts independent references to a mutable CaptureSession, a SnapshotRoot and a freely constructible SnapshotWalkReport. The current tests correctly obtain a report from that session, but the signature does not prevent a default report, a report from another root/session or stale reuse. When J2 composes the production path, retain an opaque session-bound completion token or a single helper that walks and then seals, and consider consuming/freezing the session against later source reads. This is a future composition obligation, not an assertion that a production caller currently exists.
